drills.title: Count the words
drills.prompt: Arrange the lines into a program that counts how often each word appears (TreeMap keeps the words A-Z). The two imports can go in either order, and so can the text and the map. Two lines do not belong.
lines: String text = "to be or not to be";
drills.explain: This is the counting pattern: for every word, read the old count with a default of 0 for a word not seen yet, add 1 and put it back. getOrDefault needs both the key and the default. A map holds objects, so the value type is Integer, never int. TreeMap prints its keys sorted A-Z.

drills.title: Put, get and ask
drills.prompt: Fill the blanks so the program prints the goal output.
drills.explain: put adds a key, and putting the same key again replaces its value (chai is 25, and the map still has only two keys). get returns null for a missing key; getOrDefault returns your fallback instead. containsKey asks about keys, containsValue about values, so containsValue("samosa") would be false.

drills.title: Replace, missing and merge
drills.prompt: Read the code and type exactly what it prints, one line per line of output.
drills.explain: A key is unique: the second put for pen replaced 10 with 12, and a TreeMap prints its keys sorted, so book comes first. get on a missing key gives null, with no crash. getOrDefault gives 0 for the missing key, and 0 + size() (2) is 2. merge("book", -1, Integer::sum) adds -1 to the old value 5, so one book is sold: 4.

drills.title: The first word crashes
drills.prompt: The word counter crashes while it runs, on the very first word. Click the line that crashes, then choose the fix.
code: for (String word : "to be or not to be".split(" ")) {
fixed_code: for (String word : "to be or not to be".split(" ")) {
drills.explain: The first time a word is seen, get(word) returns null (nothing stored yet). Adding 1 to null makes Java unbox it and throw NullPointerException. getOrDefault(word, 0) supplies 0 for a new word. counts.put(word, 1) would run but reset every count to 1.

drills.title: Review the AI's stock report
drills.prompt: An AI assistant wrote this stock report. It compiles and runs, but tick the real problems (there are three).

issues.text: The report is called sorted, but a HashMap does not keep its keys in any order
issues.why: Use a TreeMap for A-Z order (new TreeMap<>(stock)) or a LinkedHashMap to keep the order of insertion.

issues.text: A missing item prints Mugs in stock: null instead of 0
issues.why: get returns null for a missing key. For a count use getOrDefault("mug", 0), so the report says 0 (and an arithmetic use would not crash).

issues.text: pen and book both have 500, yet the == test never prints Same stock
issues.why: get returns Integer objects, and == compares the objects, which are different above 127. Compare values with equals: stock.get("pen").equals(stock.get("book")).

non_issues.text: stock.put("bag", 18) fails or duplicates the key because bag already exists
non_issues.why: Keys are unique. Putting an existing key simply replaces its value, which is how you update a map.

non_issues.text: The type should be Map<String, int> because the stock is a whole number
non_issues.why: Maps hold objects, so the value type must be Integer. Map<String, int> does not compile.

non_issues.text: stock should be declared as HashMap<String, Integer>
non_issues.why: Declaring Map<...> and choosing the class after new is the standard Java habit.

drills.explain: Maps hide three quiet traps: key order, null for a missing key and Integer values compared with ==. Each one compiles and gives a plausible report on a small example.
